claim: TIFM is composed of 115 metabolites at the average concentration previously observed in the IF of KrasLSL-G12D/+; Trp53fl/fl; Pdx1Cre murine PDAC tumors.
source: TIFM is composed of 115 metabolites at the average concentration previously observed in the IF of KrasLSL-G12D/+; Trp53fl/fl; Pdx1Cre (Bardeesy et al., 2006; Sullivan et al., 2019a) murine PDAC tumors.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the composition of TIFM and cites the source of the concentration data.

claim: Quantitative metabolite profiling by LC-MS confirmed that TIFM contained metabolites at expected concentrations.
source: Importantly, quantitative metabolite profiling by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) of TIFM confirmed that TIFM contained metabolites at expected concentrations (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by LC-MS measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claim: mPDAC-TIFM cells readily proliferate in TIFM culture, albeit at a slower rate than in RPMI-1640.
source: mPDAC-TIFM cells readily proliferate in TIFM culture, albeit at a slower rate than in RPMI-1640 (Figure 1D), suggesting that TIFM has the necessary nutrients to sustain PDAC cell proliferation.
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation rate measurements shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Transferring mPDAC-RPMI cells directly to TIFM results in near-complete arrest of cell growth.
source: Interestingly, while mPDAC-TIFM cells continue proliferating when transitioned directly from culture in TIFM to RPMI-1640, transferring mPDAC-RPMI cells directly to TIFM results in near-complete arrest of cell growth (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Long-term growth of mPDAC cells in standard cell culture media results in loss of key adaptations to grow under TME-nutrient stress.
source: This suggests that long-term growth of mPDAC cells in standard cell culture media results in loss of key adaptations to grow under TME-nutrient stress.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that mPDAC-RPMI cells cannot grow when transferred to TIFM.

claim: The majority of detected transcripts (12,066/16,378) are differentially expressed in the same mPDAC cells when grown in vivo compared to standard culture conditions.
source: The majority of detected transcripts (12,066/16,378) are differentially expressed in the same mPDAC cells when grown in vivo compared to standard culture conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Compared to mPDAC cells cultured in RPMI, mPDAC cells in TIFM show a strong enrichment for in vivo upregulated genes.
source: Compared to mPDAC cells cultured in RPMI, mPDAC cells in TIFM show a strong enrichment for in vivo upregulated genes (Figure 1G) and negative enrichment for genes downregulated in vivo (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figures 1G and 1H.

claim: Among the top 20 up- and downregulated curated gene signatures from MSigDB in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells compared to RPMI, most were similarly up- or downregulated in vivo compared to RPMI.
source: Lastly, among the top 20 up- and downregulated curated gene signatures from MSigDB (Mootha et al., 2003; Subramanian et al., 2005) in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells compared to RPMI, most were similarly up- or downregulated in vivo compared to RPMI (Figure 1I and Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene signature analysis shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Gene expression in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells more closely aligns with the gene expression pattern of mPDAC cells in vivo.
source: Altogether, this analysis demonstrates that gene expression in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells more closely aligns with the gene expression pattern of mPDAC cells in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple transcriptomic analyses.

claim: The main cellular processes differentiating PDAC cells growing in vivo from cells growing in TIFM are cell–cell communication, response to biotic stimuli, cell surface receptor-activated pathways, and regulation of the immune system.
source: The main cellular processes differentiating PDAC cells growing in vivo from cells growing in TIFM are cell–cell communication, response to biotic stimuli, cell surface receptor-activated pathways, and regulation of the immune system (Figure 1J and Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The amino acid deprivation gene signature is highly enriched in TIFM.
source: We focused on adaptation to amino acid deprivation, as this gene signature is highly enriched in TIFM (Figure 1K) and is similarly enriched in mPDAC cells in vivo (Figure 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Ass1 is the most differentially expressed gene in the amino acid deprivation signature.
source: Leading edge analysis (Subramanian et al., 2005) identified Ass1 as the most differentially expressed gene in this signature (Figure 1L).
evidence: The claim is supported by leading edge analysis shown in Figure 1L.

claim: ASS1 protein is upregulated in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells compared to RPMI cultured cells.
source: We further confirmed the upregulation of Argininosuccinate synthase 1 (ASS1) at the protein level by immunoblotting for ASS1 in protein extracts from TIFM and RPMI cultured mPDAC cells (Figure 1M).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 1M.

claim: Murine and human PDAC tumors show robust expression of ASS1, especially compared to the lack of expression in the untransformed exocrine pancreas.
source: Immunohistological analysis of murine and human PDAC tumors (Figure 1N) shows similarly robust expression of ASS1, especially compared to the lack of expression in the untransformed exocrine pancreas.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 1N.

claim: ASS1 is the rate-limiting enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway of the non-essential amino acid arginine.
source: ASS1 is the rate-limiting enzyme in the biosynthetic pathway of the non-essential amino acid arginine (Haines et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to established knowledge.

claim: ASS1 catalyzes the synthesis of argininosuccinate from citrulline and aspartate, which can then be converted to arginine and fumarate by argininosuccinate lyase.
source: ASS1 catalyzes the synthesis of argininosuccinate from citrulline and aspartate, which can then be converted to arginine and fumarate by argininosuccinate lyase (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim describes a known biochemical pathway and is illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: Arginine is one of the most limiting nutrients in the murine PDAC TME at 2–5 μM relative to 125 μM in plasma, a 20- to 50-fold decrease.
source: Arginine is one of the most limiting nutrients in the murine PDAC TME at 2–5 μM relative to 125 μM in plasma, a 20- to 50-fold decrease (Sullivan et al., 2019a), leaving the TME level of arginine below the reported Km for arginine transport (Closs et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous measurements.

claim: mPDAC1-TIFM cells selectively consume citrulline, but not ornithine, at a rate similar to that of arginine uptake.
source: Interestingly, we found that mPDAC1-TIFM cells selectively consume citrulline, but not ornithine, at a rate similar to that of arginine uptake (Figure 2B and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by consumption/release analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 100% of intracellular argininosuccinate and almost half of total intracellular arginine was labeled by 13C5-citrulline.
source: 100% of intracellular argininosuccinate and almost half of total intracellular arginine was labeled by 13C5-citrulline (Figure 2D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: De novo synthesis contributes a substantial fraction of cellular arginine in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells.
source: Thus, de novo synthesis contributes a substantial fraction of cellular arginine in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells, a finding consistent across multiple mPDAC cell lines in TIFM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data across multiple cell lines.

claim: Inhibiting arginine synthesis by deprivation of citrulline and ornithine from TIFM results in a 10-fold decrease of intracellular arginine in mPDAC cells.
source: Consistent with this, inhibiting arginine synthesis by deprivation of citrulline and ornithine from TIFM results in a 10-fold decrease of intracellular arginine in mPDAC cells (Figure 2F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolite measurements shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Decrease in intracellular arginine upon citrulline and ornithine deprivation is accompanied by a significant decrease in cell proliferation.
source: This decrease in intracellular arginine is accompanied by a significant decrease in cell proliferation (Figure 2G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Depletion of citrulline, but not ornithine, is the key substrate mPDAC cells require for arginine synthesis.
source: Importantly, consistent with the consumption/release (Co/Re) analysis by LC–MS (Figure 2B), individual depletion of either citrulline or ornithine further shows that depletion of citrulline, but not ornithine, is the key substrate mPDAC cells require for arginine synthesis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: Ass1 KO decreases mPDAC proliferation and this effect can be rescued by supplying additional exogenous arginine in TIFM or by re-expression of Ass1.
source: Furthermore, while we could not detect decreases in mPDAC intracellular arginine levels after eliminating extracellular arginine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), eliminating TIFM extracellular arginine completely abrogates cell growth in multiple mPDAC cell lines upon inhibition of de novo arginine synthesis (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Arginine addition almost completely rescues the inhibition of cell growth observed when transferring mPDAC-RPMI cells directly to TIFM.
source: We found arginine addition almost completely rescues the inhibition of cell growth observed when transferring mPDAC-RPMI cells directly to TIFM (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: There is a greater amount of labeled arginine in PDAC tumor tissue compared to plasma after 15N2-glutamine injection.
source: In contrast, there is a greater amount of labeled arginine in PDAC tumor tissue compared to plasma, with ~17% 15N1-arginine and ~9% 15N2-arginine in tumors (Figure 2L).
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 2L.

claim: The appearance of additional 15N enrichment in intratumoral arginine that cannot be explained by circulating labeled arginine confirms active synthesis of arginine in PDAC tumors.
source: While these non-steady-state isotope labeling experiments cannot allow us to infer the fraction of intratumoral arginine that arises from de novo synthesis in PDAC tumors (Buescher et al., 2015), the appearance of additional 15N enrichment in intratumoral arginine that cannot be explained by circulating labeled arginine confirms active synthesis of arginine in PDAC tumors, consistent with previous results (Figure 1) that PDAC tumors highly express ASS1.
evidence: The claim is an inference from isotope tracing data and is supported by citation.

claim: PDAC tumors had higher concentrations of free arginine than what is present in the TIF.
source: However, PDAC tumors had higher concentrations of free arginine than what is present in the TIF.
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolite concentration measurements.

claim: PDAC tumors accumulate higher levels of arginine than available from the local perfusate and this is at least in part driven by de novo synthesis.
source: Thus, we conclude that PDAC tumors accumulate higher levels of arginine than available from the local perfusate and that this is at least in part driven by de novo synthesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Loss of Ass1 did not affect tumor growth despite low levels of arginine in the TME.
source: We found that loss of Ass1 did not affect tumor growth despite low levels of arginine in the TME (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, B.

claim: Although arginine biosynthesis is active and upregulated in PDAC tumors, inhibiting this pathway is not detrimental for PDAC tumor growth.
source: These results suggest that, although arginine biosynthesis is active and upregulated in PDAC tumors (Figures 1M and 2L), inhibiting this pathway is not detrimental for PDAC tumor growth.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Ass1 KO does not affect tumor growth.

claim: Knockdown of Sdc1 did not affect intracellular arginine pools nor cell proliferation in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells.
source: Sdc1 knockdown did not affect intracellular arginine pools nor cell proliferation in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells (Figure 3A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolite and proliferation data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of lysosomal protein breakdown with hydroxychloroquine impairs mPDAC1-TIFM macropinocytosis rate without disrupting cell proliferation.
source: Consistent with this, pharmacological inhibition of lysosomal protein breakdown with hydroxychloroquine similarly impairs mPDAC1-TIFM macropinocytosis rate without disrupting cell proliferation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by macropinocytosis and proliferation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: Macropinocytosis does not contribute to mPDAC arginine homeostasis in TIFM, even as an adaptive mechanism upon de novo arginine synthesis inhibition.
source: Thus, we conclude that macropinocytosis does not contribute to mPDAC arginine homeostasis in TIFM, even as an adaptive mechanism upon de novo arginine synthesis inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments.

claim: Removal of arginine does not affect mPDAC intracellular arginine levels nor proliferative capacity in normal TIFM culture.
source: In normal TIFM culture, removal of arginine does not affect mPDAC intracellular arginine levels nor proliferative capacity (Figure 3D, E).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolite and proliferation data shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: Inhibition of arginine synthesis in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells leads to increased transcription of arginine transporters.
source: We found that inhibition of arginine synthesis in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells leads to increased transcription of arginine transporters (Figure 3F) and leads to an increased rate of arginine uptake by mPDAC cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Inhibition of arginine synthesis leads to an increased rate of arginine uptake by mPDAC cells.
source: We found that inhibition of arginine synthesis in TIFM cultured mPDAC cells leads to increased transcription of arginine transporters (Figure 3F) and leads to an increased rate of arginine uptake by mPDAC cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by arginine consumption data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Eliminating TIFM extracellular arginine completely abrogates cell growth in multiple mPDAC cell lines upon inhibition of de novo arginine synthesis.
source: Furthermore, while we could not detect decreases in mPDAC intracellular arginine levels after eliminating extracellular arginine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), eliminating TIFM extracellular arginine completely abrogates cell growth in multiple mPDAC cell lines upon inhibition of de novo arginine synthesis (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: mPDAC cells upregulate the uptake of extracellular arginine to cope with inhibition of arginine biosynthesis.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that mPDAC cells upregulate the uptake of extracellular arginine to cope with inhibition of arginine biosynthesis and that this could be in part mediated by the upregulation of cationic amino acid transporters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments.

claim: Human and murine PDAC tumors contain substantial myeloid compartments, including many arginase-1 expressing cells.
source: Human and murine PDAC tumors contain substantial myeloid compartments (Lee et al., 2021; Zhu et al., 2017), including many arginase-1 expressing cells (Trovato et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is a robust myeloid and arginase-1 expressing population in both murine and human PDAC.
source: We confirmed the presence of a robust myeloid and arginase-1 expressing populations in both murine (Figure 4A) and human PDAC (Figure 4B) by immunohistochemical analysis.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl tumors show robust reduction of arginase-1 expression in tumors compared to control animals.
source: Compared to control animals, Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl tumors show robust reduction of arginase-1 expression in tumors (Figure 4D) confirming most arginase-1 in tumors is myeloid in origin.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Most arginase-1 in tumors is myeloid in origin.
source: Compared to control animals, Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl tumors show robust reduction of arginase-1 expression in tumors (Figure 4D) confirming most arginase-1 in tumors is myeloid in origin.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that myeloid-specific Arg1 KO reduces tumor arginase-1 expression.

claim: Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl tumors had ~ninefold increase in IF arginine concentration and a roughly equimolar decrease in ornithine.
source: Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl tumors had ~ninefold increase in IF arginine concentration and a roughly equimolar decrease in ornithine (Figure 4E and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolite concentration measurements shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of arginase-1 with CB-1158 in mPDAC orthotopic tumors led to an increase in IF arginine compared to control tumors.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of arginase-1 with the small-molecule inhibitor CB-1158 (Steggerda et al., 2017) in mPDAC orthotopic tumors also led to an increase in IF arginine compared to control tumors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolite concentration measurements shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Arginase activity in the myeloid compartment of PDAC tumors is responsible for arginine depletion in the TME.
source: In summary, these results show that arginase activity in the myeloid compartment of PDAC tumors is responsible for arginine depletion in the TME.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from genetic and pharmacological experiments.

claim: There is no difference in PDAC cell expression of ASS1 between Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl and control tumors.
source: We first assessed expression of ASS1 and found no difference in PDAC cell expression of ASS1 between Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl and control tumors (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: There are no significant differences in labeling of tumor argininosuccinate or arginine between Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl and control animals after 15N2-glutamine infusion.
source: Further, we assessed arginine synthesis by continuous infusion of 15N2-glutamine in PDAC-bearing Lyz2-Cre+/+; Arg1fl/fl and control animals (Zaytouni et al., 2017). We did not observe significant differences in labeling of tumor argininosuccinate or arginine (Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4—source data 2), from which we conclude arginine synthesis is similarly active in PDAC tumors with arginine starved and replete TMEs.
evidence: The claim is supported by isotope tracing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Arginine synthesis is similarly active in PDAC tumors with arginine starved and replete TMEs.
source: We did not observe significant differences in labeling of tumor argininosuccinate or arginine (Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4—source data 2), from which we conclude arginine synthesis is similarly active in PDAC tumors with arginine starved and replete TMEs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from isotope tracing data.

claim: Arginine synthesis is constitutively active in PDAC tumors and does not respond to TME arginine availability.
source: Altogether, these data suggest arginine synthesis is constitutively active in PDAC tumors and does not respond to TME arginine availability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments.

claim: The TME induces substantial changes in the transcriptional state of PDAC cells compared to PDAC cells in standard culture.
source: We directly assessed the impact of the TME on the cellular state of murine PDAC cells by transcriptomic analysis. We found that the TME does indeed induce substantial changes in the transcriptional state of PDAC cells compared to PDAC cells in standard culture, consistent with the microenvironment being an important regulator of cancer cell biology (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Growth of PDAC cells in physiological nutrition causes substantial transcriptional reprogramming, pushing PDAC cells toward a more in vivo-like transcriptional state compared to non-physiological standard culture conditions.
source: Indeed, we found that growth of PDAC cells in physiological nutrition caused substantial transcriptional reprogramming, pushing PDAC cells toward a more in vivo-like transcriptional state compared to non-physiological standard culture conditions (Figure 1G, H).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis shown in Figures 1G and 1H.

claim: Modeling physiological nutrient availability substantially improves cell culture model fidelity.
source: Thus, consistent with recent studies that have incorporated physiological nutrient levels into cell culture systems (Ackermann and Tardito, 2019; Cantor et al., 2017; Muir et al., 2017; Vande Voorde et al., 2019), we have found that modeling physiological nutrient availability substantially improves cell culture model fidelity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from transcriptomic analysis and is supported by citations.

claim: ASS1 acts as a metabolic tumor suppressor and is silenced in many tumor types.
source: Aspartate limitation that arises from arginine synthesis slows nucleotide production and, ultimately tumor growth (Rabinovich et al., 2015). Thus, ASS1 acts as a metabolic tumor suppressor and is silenced in many tumor types (Lee et al., 2018), making the finding of PDAC cells synthesizing arginine initially surprising.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ASS1-silenced tumors treated with arginine deiminase to eliminate extracellular arginine acquire resistance to such therapy by reactivating ASS1 expression.
source: For example, ASS1-silenced tumors treated with arginine deiminase to eliminate extracellular arginine acquire resistance to such therapy by reactivating ASS1 expression (Rogers and Van Tine, 2019; Rogers et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Reactivation of arginine biosynthesis was shown to be necessary to support metastasis of clear cell renal cancers to the arginine limited lung environment.
source: In another example, reactivation of arginine biosynthesis was shown to be necessary to support metastasis of clear cell renal cancers to the arginine limited lung environment, whereas arginine biosynthesis was not necessary and inactive in the arginine-replete primary tumor (Sciacovelli et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: ATF4-CEBPβ-mediated upregulation of ASS1 upon amino acid stress has been shown to allow AML cells to adapt to low levels of microenvironmental arginine.
source: Lastly, ATF4-CEBPβ-mediated upregulation of ASS1 upon amino acid stress has been shown to allow AML cells to adapt to low levels of microenvironmental arginine (Crump et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In the context of microenvironmental arginine deprivation, ASS1 and arginine biosynthesis can switch their role to become tumor supportive.
source: Altogether, these findings suggest that the tumor suppressive role of arginine biosynthesis is context dependent. In the context of microenvironmental arginine deprivation, ASS1 and arginine biosynthesis can switch their role to become tumor supportive.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from multiple cited studies.

claim: Anti-tumor lymphocytes require arginine for functionality, but are not able to upregulate arginine biosynthesis upon arginine starvation.
source: For example, anti-tumor lymphocytes require arginine for functionality (Geiger et al., 2016), but are not able to upregulate arginine biosynthesis upon arginine starvation (Crump et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Microenvironmental arginine availability is known to limit immune responses in a variety of tumor types.
source: Thus, microenvironmental arginine availability is known to limit immune responses in a variety of tumor types (Murray, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Pharmacological tools to increase TME arginine have improved immunotherapeutic outcomes in a variety of murine tumor models.
source: This has led to many recent efforts to develop pharmacological tools to increase TME arginine (Canale et al., 2021; Steggerda et al., 2017), which have improved immunotherapeutic outcomes in a variety of murine tumor models (Canale et al., 2021; Miret et al., 2019; Sosnowska et al., 2021; Steggerda et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Low arginine availability impairs anti-tumor immunity in PDAC and raising TME arginine levels can improve tumor immune surveillance and response to immunotherapy.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, low arginine availability does impair anti-tumor immunity in PDAC and raising TME arginine levels can improve tumor immune surveillance and response to immunotherapy (Canè et al., 2023; Menjivar et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Myeloid cells were found to be the major glucose consuming cell type in a variety of tumor types.
source: For example, in addition to the role we have found for myeloid cells in limiting TME arginine, myeloid cells were also found to be the major glucose consuming cell type in a variety of tumor types (Reinfeld et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Fibroblasts have been shown to regulate levels of key metabolites in the TME, such as amino acids and lipids.
source: Fibroblasts have been shown to also regulate levels of key metabolites in the TME (Sherman et al., 2017), such as amino acids (Francescone et al., 2021; Sousa et al., 2016) and lipids (Auciello et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tumor innervating neurons were shown to regulate availability of amino acids in the TME.
source: In addition, tumor innervating neurons were also shown to regulate availability of amino acids in the TME (Banh et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.
